topic: Chemical Sequence of Anthropogenic Ocean Acidification
questionText:
Arrange the chemical reaction steps illustrating how rising atmospheric CO2 causes ocean acidification:
(I) Anthropogenic fossil fuel emissions elevate atmospheric CO2 concentrations above 420 ppm
(II) Gaseous CO2 dissolves across the ocean surface, forming weak Carbonic Acid: CO2 + H2O <-> H2CO3
(III) Carbonic acid dissociates into Bicarbonate and free Hydrogen ions: H2CO3 <-> H+ + HCO3-, driving down oceanic pH
(IV) Excess free Hydrogen ions bind with free Carbonate ions (CO3(2-)), depleting the carbonate saturation needed by corals and shellfish to build calcium carbonate (CaCO3) shells

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: I -> II -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Chemical Sequence of Anthropogenic Ocean Acidification.

options.text: I -> III -> II -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: IV -> II -> III -> I
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: II -> I -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for International Relations and Environment (Chemical Sequence of Anthropogenic Ocean Acidification):
I -> II -> III -> IV

Detailed Analysis:
Ocean acidification sequence: atmospheric CO2 dissolution, carbonic acid formation, proton release lowering pH, and carbonate ion depletion starving calcifying organisms.
Hence, Option D is correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

Match the international Resin Identification Code (RIC) in List I with its chemical polymer in List II:

List I:
(A) Number 1 (PET / PETE)
(B) Number 2 (HDPE)
(C) Number 3 (PVC)
(D) Number 5 (PP)

List II:
(I) Polyethylene Terephthalate (Clear beverage bottles, polyester fibers)
(II) High-Density Polyethylene (Milk jugs, shampoo bottles, detergent tubs)
(III) Polyvinyl Chloride (Plumbing pipes, cable insulation, window frames)
(IV) Polypropylene (Bottle caps, drinking straws, microwaveable food containers)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
1 is PET (water bottles), 2 is HDPE (milk jugs), 3 is PVC (pipes), 4 is LDPE (bags), 5 is PP (caps), 6 is PS (thermocol), and 7 is Other.
Hence, Option A is correct.
Hence, option (B) is the correct match.

questionText:
Match the landmark Supreme Court environmental case in List I with its legal principle in List II:

List I:
(A) M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak 1987)
(B) Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. UOI (1996)
(C) M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Taj Trapezium Case 1996)
(D) Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar (1991)

List II:
(I) Formulated the doctrine of 'Absolute Liability' for hazardous and inherently dangerous industrial enterprises
(II) Integrated the 'Precautionary Principle' and 'Polluter Pays Principle' as part of the law of the land under Article 21
(III) Mandated coal-to-gas transition and ordered polluting industries in the Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ) to relocate to protect Taj Mahal marble
(IV) Held that the right to live includes the right of enjoyment of pollution-free water and air for full enjoyment of life under Article 21

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Oleum gas leak established Absolute Liability; Vellore tanneries adopted Precautionary/PPP doctrines; TTZ protected the Taj Mahal; and Subhash Kumar recognized clean water/air under Art 21.
Hence, Option B is correct.
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.

topic: Environment Protection Act 1986 as Umbrella Legislation
questionText:
Arrange the chemical reaction steps illustrating how rising atmospheric CO2 causes ocean acidification:
(I) Anthropogenic fossil fuel emissions elevate atmospheric CO2 concentrations above 420 ppm
(II) Gaseous CO2 dissolves across the ocean surface, forming weak Carbonic Acid: CO2 + H2O <-> H2CO3
(III) Carbonic acid dissociates into Bicarbonate and free Hydrogen ions: H2CO3 <-> H+ + HCO3-, driving down oceanic pH
(IV) Excess free Hydrogen ions bind with free Carbonate ions (CO3(2-)), depleting the carbonate saturation needed by corals and shellfish to build calcium carbonate (CaCO3) shells

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: I -> III -> II -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: IV -> II -> III -> I
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: I -> II -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: II -> I -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Ocean acidification sequence: atmospheric CO2 dissolution, carbonic acid formation, proton release lowering pH, and carbonate ion depletion starving calcifying organisms.
Hence, Option D is correct.
Hence, option (C) is correct.
